In mathematics, the '''effective topos''' <math>{\mathsf{Eff}}</math> introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Martin|last=Hyland|authorlink=Martin Hyland|year=1982}} captures the mathematical idea of [[computability|effectivity]] within the [[category theory|category theoretical]] framework.

==Preliminaries==
===Kleene realizability===
The [[topos]] is based on the [[Partial_combinatory_algebra|partial combinatory algebra]] given by [[Stephen Kleene|Kleene's]] first algebra <math>{\mathcal{K}}_1</math>. In Kleene's notion of [[Realizability#Example:_Kleene's_1945-realizability|recursive realizability]], any [[Predicate (mathematical logic)|predicate]] is assigned realizing numbers, i.e. a [[subset]] of <math>{\mathbb N}</math>. The extremal propositions are <math>\top</math> and <math>\bot</math>, realized by <math>{\mathbb N}</math> and <math>\{\}</math>. However in general, this process assigns more data to a proposition than just a binary [[truth value]].

A formula with <math>k</math> [[free variable]]s will give rise to a map in <math>(\mathcal P{\mathbb N})^{{\mathbb N}^k}</math> the values of which are the subsets of corresponding realizing numbers.

===Realizability topoi===
<math>{\mathsf{Eff}}</math> is a prime example of a [[realizability]] topos. These are a class of [[elementary topoi]] with an [[intuitionistic logic|intuitionistic]] internal logic and fulfilling a form of [[dependent choice]]. They are generally not Grothendieck topoi.

In particular, the effective topos is <math>{\mathsf{RT}}({\mathcal{K}}_1)</math>. Other realizability topos constructions can be said to abstract away some aspects played by <math>{\mathbb N}</math> here.

==Definition==

There are several ways to construct the effective topos, for example, via the notion of tripos, or as the [[ex/reg completion]] of the category of [[Assembly (realizability)|assemblies]]. The following is a fully unfolded explicit definition.{{r|van-oosten|p=115}}

An object of the effective topos is a set <math>X</math> equipped with a function <math>E : X^2 \to \mathcal{P}(\N)</math> satisfying certain conditions. We denote <math>n \in E(x, y)</math> by <math>n \Vdash x = y</math>. (The notation is not standardized; the usage of the <math>=</math> symbol overloads its normal meaning, similarly to the notation <math>P(X = Y)</math> in [[probability theory]].) Informally, this means that <math>n</math> is a computational witness, or ''realizer'' of the equality <math>x = y</math>. The conditions to be satisfied are the following:

* There must exist a program <math>e</math> such that for all <math>n \in \N</math> and <math>x, y \in X</math>, if <math>n \Vdash x = y</math> then the output of <math>e</math> on <math>n</math>, i.e., <math>\phi_e(n)</math> (where <math>\phi_e</math> is the <math>e</math>-th [[partial computable function]]), is defined, and <math>\phi_e(n) \Vdash y = x</math>. In short, <math>e</math> takes a realizer of <math>x = y</math> and outputs a realizer of <math>y = x</math> (for all <math>x, y</math>). (Note that <math>e</math> cannot depend on <math>x, y</math>, and it only receives the realizer of <math>x = y</math> as input, without further information on <math>x</math> and <math>y</math>.)
* Similarly, there must exist a program which takes a realizer of <math>x = y</math> and a realizer of <math>y = z</math>, and outputs a realizer of <math>x = z</math> (for all <math>x, y, z</math>).

A realizer of <math>x = x</math> will be called more simply a realizer of <math>x</math>.

A ''functional relation'' from an object <math>X</math> to an object <math>Y</math> is a function <math>f : X \times Y \to \mathcal{P}(\N)</math>, again satisfying certain conditions. We suggestively denote <math>n \in f(x, y)</math> by <math>n \Vdash f(x) = y</math> (again, this is a special notation; <math>f(x)</math> has no meaning by itself). This informally means that <math>n</math> realizes the fact that <math>f</math> sends <math>x</math> to <math>y</math>, or “realizes <math>f(x) = y</math>”. The conditions are the following:

* There exists a program which takes a realizer of <math>f(x) = y</math> and outputs a realizer of <math>x</math> and a realizer of <math>y</math> (for all <math>x \in X, y \in Y</math>).
* There exists a program which takes a realizer of <math>f(x) = y</math> and realizers of <math>x = x'</math> and <math>y = y'</math>, and outputs a realizer of <math>f(x') = y'</math> (for all <math>x, x', y, y'</math>).
* There exists a program which takes realizers of <math>f(x) = y</math> and <math>f(x) = y'</math>, and outputs a realizer of <math>y = y'</math> (for all <math>x, y, y'</math>).
* There exists a program <math>e</math> such that for all <math>x \in X</math> and for all realizer <math>n</math> of <math>x</math>, there exists some <math>y \in Y</math> such that the output <math>\phi_e(n)</math> realizes <math>f(x) = y</math>.

Suppose <math>f</math> is a functional relation from <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math> and <math>g</math> is a functional relation from <math>Y</math> to <math>Z</math>. The composition <math>g \circ f</math> is the functional relation from <math>X</math> to <math>Z</math> defined by letting the realizers of <math>(g \circ f)(x) = z</math> be the codes of pairs <math>(r, s)</math> such that, for some <math>y \in Y</math>, we have <math>r \Vdash f(x) = y</math> and <math>s \Vdash g(y) = z</math>. The identity functional relation <math>\operatorname{id}</math> on an object <math>X</math> is defined by letting the realizers of <math>\operatorname{id}(x) = y</math> be just the realizers of <math>x = y</math>.

The morphisms from <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math> in the effective topos are the functional relations from <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math>, quotiented to identify <math>f</math> and <math>g</math> when there exists a program which maps realizers of <math>f(x) = y</math> to realizers of <math>g(x) = y</math> (for all <math>x, y</math>), and another program which maps realizers of <math>g(x) = y</math> to realizers of <math>f(x) = y</math>. Composition of morphisms is induced on the quotients by composition on the level of functional relations, and likewise for identity morphisms.

== Relationship to assemblies ==

The effective topos arises as a completion of the simpler category of [[Assembly (realizability)|assemblies]].

An assembly is a set <math>X</math> equipped with a function <math>R : X \to \mathcal{P}(\N)</math>. We denote <math>n \in R(x)</math> by <math>n \Vdash x</math>, read “<math>n</math> realizes <math>x</math>”. Every assembly <math>X</math> can be construed as an object of the effective topos, by declaring that <math>n</math> realizes <math>x = y</math> when <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> are actually equal and <math>n</math> realizes them in the assembly <math>X</math>. (Thus, the realizers of <math>x</math> in <math>X</math> as an object of the effective topos, i.e., the realizers of <math>x = x</math>, are exactly the realizers of <math>x</math> in <math>X</math> as an assembly.)

A morphism of assemblies <math>f : X \to Y</math> is a function <math>f : X \to Y</math> between the underlying sets such that there exists a program, independent of <math>x \in X</math>, which maps realizers of <math>x</math> to realizers of <math>f(x)</math>. Such a morphism gives rise to a morphism in the effective topos, represented by the functional relation (still denoted <math>f</math>) where <math>f(x) = y</math> is realized if and only if <math>f(x)</math> is actually equal to <math>y</math>, and then the realizers of <math>f(x) = y</math> are the pairs of a realizer of <math>x</math> and a realizer of <math>y</math>.

This correspondence makes the category of assemblies a [[full subcategory]] of the effective topos.

The category of sets is a full subcategory of the category of assemblies, via the functor <math>\nabla</math> that maps a set <math>X</math> to the assembly with underlying set <math>X</math> where every element is realized by every natural number. In particular, the category of sets is also a full subcategory of the effective topos.{{r|van-oosten|p=117}}

== Categorical operations in the effective topos ==

The effective topos is an [[elementary topos]] with [[natural numbers object]]. This means that it supports a number of standard categorical constructions, which are explicitly performed as follows.

* The [[initial object]] is the empty assembly.
* The [[terminal object]] is the unit assembly, a singleton where the unique element is realized by every natural number.
* The [[natural numbers object]] is <math>\N</math> where each natural number is realized only by itself.
* The [[Product (category theory)|product]] of two objects <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> is the Cartesian product of sets <math>X \times Y</math> where a realizer of <math>(x, y)</math> in <math>X \times Y</math> is the code of a pair of a realizer of <math>x</math> and a realizer of <math>y</math>.
* The [[coproduct]] of <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> is the coproduct of sets <math>X + Y</math> where a realizer of <math>x \in X</math> in <math>X + Y</math> is the code of a pair of 0 and a realizer of <math>x</math> in <math>X</math>, and a realizer of <math>y \in Y</math> in <math>X + Y</math> is the code of a pair of 1 and a realizer of <math>y</math> in <math>Y</math>.
* The [[subobject classifier]] <math>\Omega</math> is <math>\mathcal{P}(\N)</math> where a realizer of <math>P = Q</math> is a pair of a program which returns an element of <math>Q</math> given an element of <math>P</math>, and a program which returns an element of <math>P</math> given an element of <math>Q</math>. It is ''not'' (isomorphic to) an assembly.

{{expand section|small=no|with=action of the universal properties of the above on morphisms; equalizers, coequalizers, exponentials, image factorizations|date=May 2026}}

==Properties==
===Relation to Sets===
Some objects exhibit a rather trivial existence predicate depending only on the validity of the equality relation "<math>=</math>" of sets, so that valid equality maps to the top set <math>\mathbb N</math> and rejected equality maps to <math>\{\}</math>. This gives rise to a [[full and faithful functor]] <math>\nabla\colon{\mathsf{Sets}}\to{\mathsf{Eff}}</math> out of the [[category of sets]], which has the finite-limit preserving global sections functor <math>\Gamma</math> as its [[left-adjoint]].
This factors through a finite-limit preserving, full and faithful embedding <math>\omega</math>-<math>{\mathsf{Sets}}\to{\mathsf{Eff}}</math>.

===NNO===
The topos has a [[natural numbers object]] <math>N=\langle{\mathbb N}, E_{\mathbb N}\rangle</math> with simply <math>E_{\mathbb N}(n)=\{n\}</math>.
Sentences true about <math>N</math> are exactly the recursively realized sentences of [[Heyting arithmetic]] <math>{\mathsf{HA}}</math>.

Now arrows <math>N\to N</math> may be understood as the total recursive functions and this also holds internally for <math>N^N</math>. The latter is the pair given by total recursive functions <math>\mathrm{TR}</math> and a relation such that <math>E_\mathrm{TR}(f)</math> is the set of codes <math>e\in {\mathbb N}</math> for <math>f</math>. The  latter is a subset of the naturals but not just a singleton, since there are several indices computing the same recursive function. So here the second entry of the objects represent the realizing data.

With <math>N</math> and functions from and to it, as well as with simple rules for the equality relations when forming finite products <math>\times</math>, one may now more broadly define the hereditarily effective operations.
Again one may think of functions in <math>N^N</math> as given by indices and their equality is determined by the objects that compute the same function. This equality clearly puts a constraint on <math>N^{(N^N)}</math>, as these functions come out to be only those computable functions that also properly respect the mentioned equality in their domain. Et cetera.
The situation for general <math>\langle X, E_X\rangle\to \langle Y, E_Y\rangle</math>, equality (in the sense of the <math>E</math>'s) in domain and image must be respected.

====Properties and principles====
With this, one may validate [[Markov's principle]] <math>{\mathrm{MP}}</math> and the [[Church%27s_thesis_(constructive_mathematics)#Extended_Church's_thesis|extended Church's principle]] <math>{\mathrm{ECT}}_0</math> (and a second-order variant thereof), which come down to simple statement about object such as <math>N^N</math> or <math>(1+1)^N</math>. These imply <math>{\mathrm{CT}}_0</math> and [[independence of premise]] <math>{\mathrm{IP}}_0</math>. 

A choice principle <math>N^N</math> related to [[L. E. J. Brouwer|Brouwerian]] weak continuity fails.
From any object, there are only countably many arrows to <math>N</math>.
<math>\Omega^N</math> fulfills a uniformity principle.
<math>N</math> is not the countable coproduct of copies of <math>1</math>. This topos is not a category of sheaves.

===Analysis===
The object <math>\langle{\mathbb Q}^{\mathbb N}, E_{{\mathbb Q}^{\mathbb N}}\rangle</math> is effective in a formal sense and from it one may define computable [[Cauchy sequence]]s. Through a quotient, the topos has a real numbers object which has [[Indecomposability (intuitionistic logic)|no non-trivial]] decidable subobject. With choice, the notion of Dedekind reals coincides with the Cauchy one.

====Properties and principles====
Analysis here corresponds to the [[Andrey Markov Jr.|recursive school]] of constructivism. 
It rejects the claim that <math>x\le 0\lor 0\le x</math> would hold for all reals <math>x</math>. Formulations of the [[intermediate value theorem]] fail and all functions from the reals to the reals are provenly [[Continuous function|continuous]]. A [[Specker sequence]] exists and then [[Bolzano-Weierstrass|Bolzano–Weierstrass]] fails.
